## Overview When a later preload rank exits after READY, the launcher can stay blocked joining an earlier, healthy rank and leave sibling daemons running. Supervise every rank through startup and serving, preserve the original failure status, and clean up the entire group. Related to #56049. ## Claims - Detect any rank's exit after READY without waiting for an earlier rank to exit first. - Preserve the failing rank's status before terminating siblings; report signal deaths as `128 + signal` and unexpected clean exits as status 1. - Terminate and reap started ranks on failure or launcher signals, escalating to `kill()` after a shared ten-second grace period. Stop the health endpoint during cleanup. ## Validation ### October 29 CI follow-up Upstream #64474 has now merged. This branch includes its original main commit `ee1056b3179adfd4523dfdceb87b0a079801b6f4`, with all four PR files byte-identical to the previous `6fdaec31fa3d` revision. On the exact merged head `2b53258c4ddc`, the same three B300 TP2 CLI fault scenarios passed again (**3 passed, 65 deselected, 70.19s**); all four feature-file hooks and merge commit hooks passed. On this same head, the hosted documentation build passed. Isotr0py requested `/ci retry`; [Buildkite #98305](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98305) reran the previously failing L4 Distributed Preload step successfully, with successful bootstrap, image-build and pre-commit checks. This is a targeted rerun, not a claim that the complete GPU matrix was rerun. Isotr0py enabled auto-merge; the last observed PR state remains OPEN. Current head: `2b53258c4ddcf89dc839228520a35cf8d669d906`; [test-only incremental diff](https://github.com/liusy58/vllm/compare/d7c8b710df9b194aae75cd87e4469d1e759a4457...6fdaec31fa3d8e7fbe23e87e8d8e4a226c5352b6). Isotr0py requested CI and marked the PR ready for review. The CI bot merged main `34091a07c7` as `d7c8b710df9b`. GitHub currently associates Isotr0py’s October 29 approval with `d7c8b710df9b194aae75cd87e4469d1e759a4457`. That approval predates the test-only follow-up below and is not represented as approval of the new revision or human-run validation. [Buildkite #98245, L4 Distributed Preload](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98245#01a18702-498d-499f-b395-803a9b0903fe) reported `2 failed, 3 passed` on `d7c8b710df9b`: the startup and serving tests raised `psutil.ZombieProcess` while reading `child.cmdline()`, before fault injection. A short-lived child can exit between enumeration and command-line inspection. The unresponsive-sibling case, existing TP2/EP model case and D2D warmup case passed in that job. The follow-up catches `psutil.NoSuchProcess` (including `ZombieProcess`) only while identifying live spawn children. It retains the exact two-rank requirement, launcher-aliveness/deadline checks, exit code 137 and sibling-reaping assertions. No new retry, skip, timeout relaxation or production change. - Deterministic real-process reproduction: extract the checked-in discovery block with Python AST, start two real multiprocessing spawn workers, and leave a third exited child unreaped using `waitid(WEXITED | WNOWAIT)`. On `d7c8b710df9b`, exit 1 with `psutil.ZombieProcess` at `cmdline()`; with the fix, exit 0 and the selected PID set equals exactly the two live workers. No mocks; all created processes are reaped afterwards. - B300 TP2, same three real CLI fault scenarios on `6fdaec31fa3d` after the fix: **3 passed, 65 deselected, 69.53s**. The unmodified merged head also passed locally in 86.19s; this does not erase the independently reproduced CI race. - Changed-file and commit hooks: passed. Local runs used GPUs 1 and 2, the existing PyTorch 2.13/cu130 environment and process-local CUDA 13.4 compatibility libraries. No checkpoint, assertion or shared-environment changes. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. \ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/liusy/codex-runtime/cuda-compat-13-4/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k preload_rank_failure -q ``` The [documentation build on the bot merge](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35493186/) separately failed on seven MiniMax-M3 AMD docstring cross-references (`head`, `:n`, `r`). All three affected files are byte-identical to the merged main. This was tracked by #64469 and fixed by the now-merged #64474, which is included through the upstream merge described above. No duplicate implementation was added. The included upstream fix is confirmed by the successful [hosted documentation build](https://vllm--63692.org.readthedocs.build/en/63692/); the targeted L4 revalidation also passed as recorded above. ### Original feature validation NVIDIA B300, real `vllm preload`, `facebook/opt-125m`, TP2. The three fault-injection cases kill the later rank during startup, after READY, and after READY with a sibling stopped by SIGSTOP. Only children created by the test are signalled, and final cleanup checks that no sibling is alive. | Check | Before | With fix | |---|---|---| | Same scenarios after merging main 2fb320d830 | 3 failed, 119.26s: same exit-code failure and two 30-second timeouts | 3 passed, 119.12s | | Current-main existing weight-cache unit cases | — | 60 passed, 48.26s | | Qwen3.5 ordinary + MTP model-output regression | — | 2 passed, 288.13s | | Changed-file and commit hooks | — | Passed | All passing results above are from head 6a5f3a50df after merging main 2fb320d830. The Qwen3.5 ordinary and MTP cases cover ordinary loading, disk fallback, IPC attachment and warm restart with the existing suite's configuration and assertions. An initial attempt failed when another user's workload occupied the selected GPU during the run: vLLM reported 61.77 GiB free against a 78.68 GiB IPC-engine budget. The unchanged tests passed on an idle GPU; the failed logs are retained. Runs emitted torch deprecation warnings. No multi-node or ROCm validation is claimed. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5,6 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k preload_rank_failure -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'not cold_start and not d2d_warmup and not preload_rank_failure' -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'cold_start_and_warm_restart and qwen' -q ``` For the new baseline run, the exact proposed test file was copied to `tests/model_executor/model_loader/_codex_supervision_baseline.py` in the compressed-FP8 worktree, whose `vllm/entrypoints/cli/preload.py` was verified byte-identical to main 2fb320d830. Running the first command against that temporary file yielded: ```text startup: AssertionError: assert 247 == (128 + SIGKILL) serving: subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... timed out after 30 seconds unresponsive-sibling: subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... timed out after 30 seconds 3 failed, 65 deselected, 14 warnings in 119.26s ``` The proposed source with the same tests yielded `3 passed, 65 deselected, 14 warnings in 119.12s`. Both runs used real CLI subprocesses and weights; baseline failures are expected reproductions, not skipped tests. ## Details The old serving path joins processes in creation order, so failure of a later rank does not wake a join on an earlier live rank. Startup also derives the exit status after terminating siblings, losing the original signal status. One supervision loop now checks all exits; after readiness it waits on process sentinels. A `finally` block cleans up the processes that actually started, including partial startup and explicit launcher shutdown. This is launcher failure handling, separate from the engine-side daemon-loss detection merged in #62734. It does not add automatic engine restart or the roadmap's proposed `--supervise` serving mode. The merge preserves the daemon-to-daemon seed configuration from #63088 and reuses the current test helper's log collection. The regression is selected by the existing distributed preload test steps; their dependencies now include the launcher source. The preload guide documents shutdown, failure status, and stale socket behavior after forced termination. No scheduler/model-runner changes or steady-state GPU synchronization. Duplicate checks on October 26 covered #56049 and its comments and open PR searches for preload supervision, rank exit, and weight-cache shutdown. No existing PR implements this launcher fix; #62734 addresses the separate engine lifetime contract, and #63088 adds daemon-to-daemon seeding. AI assistance: Codex implemented, merged, and ran the recorded validation at the submitter's request. The maintainer approval and subsequent test-only repair are distinguished above. No human-run tests or completed approval of the new repair are asserted. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses process sentinels and the existing launcher; no model-runner changes. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Real CLI before/after tests, existing units, earlier model-output regressions, and limits recorded above. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changed-file hooks passed; preload docs and CI dependencies updated. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Motivation, duplicate checks, commands, evidence, limitations and AI disclosure included.

@@ -281,10 +281,18 @@ threat model.
 
 - Each GPU's socket path is guarded by an exclusive lock file, so a second
   daemon for the same GPU fails fast instead of clobbering the live socket.
-- `vllm preload` reports readiness once every rank is serving; if any rank
-  dies during startup, the remaining ranks are terminated and the command
-  exits with that rank's exit code.
+- `vllm preload` reports readiness once every rank is serving. If any rank
+  exits during startup or serving, the launcher terminates and reaps the
+  remaining ranks, stops its health endpoint, and exits with a nonzero status.
+  The failing rank's nonzero exit code is preserved. Signal failures use
+  `128 + signal number` (for example, 137 for `SIGKILL`); an unexpected clean
+  rank exit is reported as status 1. Restart the entire preload group before
+  attaching new engines.
 - `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` to the `vllm preload` process terminates all daemon
-  ranks, which unlinks their sockets and releases the GPU memory.
+  ranks and exits with status 130/143.
+- In either shutdown path, ranks that do not stop within ten seconds are
+  killed and reaped, releasing their GPU memory. A forcibly
+  terminated rank may leave a stale socket; the next daemon replaces it
+  after acquiring the per-GPU lock.
 
 See [vllm preload](../cli/preload.md) for the full CLI reference.

@@ -133,6 +135,53 @@ def _stop(self) -> None:
         shutil.rmtree(self.socket_dir, ignore_errors=True)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.distributed(num_gpus=2)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "after_ready,stop_sibling",
+    [(False, False), (True, False), (True, True)],
+    ids=["startup", "serving", "unresponsive-sibling"],
+)
+def test_preload_rank_failure_stops_launcher_and_siblings(after_ready, stop_sibling):
+    """A failed later rank must not leave preload waiting on an earlier rank."""
+    children: list[psutil.Process] = []
+    with WeightCacheDaemon(
+        "facebook/opt-125m",
+        tp_size=2,
+        extra_args=["--disable-flashinfer-autotune"],
+    ) as daemon:
+        try:
+            assert daemon._proc is not None
+            parent = psutil.Process(daemon._proc.pid)
+            deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
+            while len(children) != 2:
+                assert daemon._proc.poll() is None, "preload exited before spawning"
+                children = []
+                for child in parent.children():
+                    try:
+                        if "spawn_main" in " ".join(child.cmdline()):
+                            children.append(child)
+                    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
+                        # Short-lived children can exit before cmdline is read.
+                        continue
+                assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "daemon ranks did not spawn"
+                time.sleep(0.1)
+            if after_ready:
+                daemon.wait_until_ready()
+            if stop_sibling:
+                # A stopped process cannot handle SIGTERM; cleanup must escalate.
+                children[0].send_signal(signal.SIGSTOP)
+            children[-1].send_signal(signal.SIGKILL)
+            assert daemon._proc.wait(timeout=30) == 128 + signal.SIGKILL
+            _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(children, timeout=10)
+            assert not alive, "preload left sibling ranks running"
+        finally:
+            # Also clean up on the unfixed launcher, which waits indefinitely.
+            for child in children:
+                if child.is_running():
+                    child.kill()
+            psutil.wait_procs(children, timeout=10)
+

+                    # Preserve the failure before terminating healthy siblings.
+                    # A clean rank exit is also unexpected while serving.
+                    failure = next((code for p in dead if (code := p.exitcode)), 1)
+                    exit_code = 128 - failure if failure < 0 else failure
+                    break
+                if ready == expected_ready:
+                    wait([p.sentinel for p in procs], timeout=1.0)
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    ready.add(ready_queue.get(timeout=1.0))
+                except queue.Empty:
+                    continue
+                if ready == expected_ready:
+                    health_state.mark_ready()
+                    socket_dir_msg = (
+                        args.weight_cache_socket_dir or "the default socket dir"
+                    )
+                    logger.info_once(
+                        "===== Weight cache daemon READY: node %d/%d serving %d "
+                        "local rank(s) x %d role(s) in %s =====",
+                        node_rank,
+                        nnodes,
+                        local_world_size,
+                        len(groups),
+                        socket_dir_msg,
+                    )
+        finally:
+            if health_server is not None:
+                health_server.should_exit = True
+            for proc in started:
+                if proc.is_alive():
+                    proc.terminate()
+            deadline = time.monotonic() + 10.0
+            for proc in started:
+                proc.join(timeout=max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
+            for proc in started:
+                if proc.is_alive():
+                    proc.kill()
+            for proc in started:
+                proc.join()
+            if health_thread is not None:
+                health_thread.join()
+            ready_queue.close()
